short: Jewish resistance fighters launched a month-long armed revolt against German forces liquidating the Warsaw Ghetto.
full:
On 19 April 1943, German troops entered the Warsaw Ghetto to deport its surviving inhabitants to the Treblinka extermination camp. They were met with coordinated armed resistance by Jewish paramilitary organisations, primarily the Jewish Fighting Organization (ŻOB) and the Jewish Military Union (ŻZW). Armed with smuggled weapons, improvised explosives, and a deep sense of desperation, the fighters inflicted early casualties and forced the initial German columns to retreat.

The German commander, SS-Brigadeführer Jürgen Stroop, responded by systematically burning the ghetto block by block to flush out the defenders from their bunkers. The uprising was eventually crushed on 16 May 1943, marked by the symbolic destruction of the Great Synagogue of Warsaw. Although doomed from the start, the revolt became a powerful symbol of Jewish resistance against the Holocaust and inspired further uprisings across occupied Eastern Europe.
